summary: Zhao Luo specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Tibetology. Luo studied under Sen Wang and was attested as a scholar at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.

Zhaohua Yang works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Yang held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (faculty, attested 2018), and taught Kevin Buckelew.

Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Ji earned a Ph.D. in sociology from the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences by 2007 and was an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Liu completed an MA at the University of Munich by 2005 and an MA at Lanzhou University by 2009.
Zhengyan is a religious studies and Buddhist studies figure who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.

Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College in 1947 and under Yin Shun in 1952. Zhenhua taught Chien Y. Hsu and was manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD at Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002). Yao served as Associate Professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2004) and Professor at the University of Hong Kong (2005).

Zhiru Ng works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Ng completed an MA under Luis Oscar Gómez at the University of Michigan and a PhD under Robert M. Gimello at the University of Arizona.

Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist and religious studies. Shi earned an MA from the University of Michigan (1993) and a PhD from the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello, and was Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

Zhiyi Yang is a sinologist who studied at Peking University and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Martin Kern. Yang held posts at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. Cui earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, later serving as teaching consultant (教學顧問) there (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was an archaeologist who studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956). Zhang later served as director (所長) of the Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji. Jiang worked at Peking University (~1978–1980), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1980–2002), and Soka University (~1999).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. Dao founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015). Li was also affiliated with the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science as a 特別研究員DC (attested 2015).

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Gimnázium (-1895) and Eötvös Loránd University (1895–1900), and later taught Lajos Ligeti.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and Gyuto Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Dechen Nyingpo. He served as Abbot of Ganden Shartse (1937–1946) and Rektor of CIHTS (1967–1971).

Zongsan Mou (1909–1995) was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. Mou held appointments at Tunghai University, the University of Hong Kong, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

Zsóka Gelle is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Vienna. Gelle held positions at Dharma Gate Buddhist College, the University of Vienna, and Eötvös Loránd University.

Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was an active figure in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. Tachibana studied under Kozui Otani (~1907–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1910–1912).
